questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to choose the best VR headset for video games
Why VR can be harmful for people with fears
How prisons in Spain are designed and run
How VR is being used to help with serious problems
questions.why: Rob says they'll hear how VR is tackling problems like domestic violence and helping people overcome phobias.

questions.q: Why do scientists and therapists find VR useful, according to Sam?
options: It is cheap and easy for anyone to use
The experience feels very intense and real
It lets people forget their problems completely
It works without any help from a therapist
questions.why: Sam says users describe VR as intense, and it's this intensity that therapists use to help people.

questions.q: How does Sam feel about heights?
options: She isn't very comfortable with them
She loves climbing tall buildings
She has never been afraid of them
She only fears them when flying
questions.why: Sam says, 'if like me, you're not very good with heights…'

questions.q: How does the Oxford VR 'Fear of Heights' system work?
options: Users visit a clinic and climb a real rope
A therapist takes users to tall buildings
Users do tasks at home, going ever higher
Users watch videos of other people climbing
questions.why: At home you put on a headset and are guided through tasks moving you higher, like a lift, then a rope.

questions.q: According to Professor Daniel Freeman, why does VR help people drop their defences?
options: Because the headset makes them feel sleepy
They know the height isn't really there
Because a doctor stays with them the whole time
Because they forget that it's a simulation
questions.why: He says a person is more able to drop their defences 'because they know there's no real height there'.

questions.q: Who uses the 'virtual embodiment' project in Barcelona?
options: Victims of crime who want to feel safer
Police officers learning to arrest people
Children who are afraid of the dark
Prisoners convicted of domestic violence
questions.why: Rob says it's used in prisons with men convicted of domestic violence.

questions.q: What does the Barcelona VR project make the prisoners experience?
options: What it's like to be a prison guard
What life will be like after prison
Abuse from their victims' point of view
What it's like to be a famous person
questions.why: It gives the men the experience of abuse in the first person – their insults turned back on them.

questions.q: What results does Dr Mavi Sanchez-Vives report?
options: More prisoners fit back into society after prison
Prisoners refuse to use the VR headsets at all
The project has now closed because it failed
Prisoners say they enjoy the experience very much
questions.why: She reports more and more prisoners successfully reintegrating into their communities after release.
